title_guess: Headline inflation vs core inflation: the index basket with and without food and fuel, why 'headline', and India's headline measure
recurring_cast: segmented_bar (the inflation index drawn as one horizontal strip cut into seven pastel blocks, each a component of the basket)
two 'INFLATION' row labels, one per bar
FOOD and FUEL blocks inside both bars
running_examples: no number example: the whole video works on the shape of one basket bar, full (headline) vs trimmed of food and fuel (core)
on screen and spoken: WPI was India's headline measure till 2014; CPI-Combined since February 2015

best_moments.why: red crosses land on the FUEL and FOOD blocks of the lower bar, then the crossed blocks drop out and the bar closes up shorter: core inflation defined by subtraction, with no sentence on screen
two black frames span both stacked bars around the same two blocks, with one 'highly volatile & transitory' note under them: the same components are picked out in both copies before they are named
after the cut, the full bar gets a blue HEADLINE chip and the short bar a purple CORE chip, so the two terms are two visible lengths of the same basket
two newspaper front pages with 'inflation' circled send arrows down to the word HEADLINE: the name explained by where the number is printed (BIE must redraw as generic papers)

weak_moments.why: the canvas stays still for about 34 s (31-65 s) while the narrator gives the causes of food and fuel swings (transitory factors, the season's rain) and the economists' worry; no price line jumps, no rain cloud
the key comparison (headline = total inflation, core = long-run trend) is spoken over an unchanged canvas for about 23 s; a jumpy headline line against a smooth core line would show it
the 'highly volatile & transitory in nature' label appears about 12 s before 'transitory' and 35 s before 'highly volatile' are spoken
real newspaper mastheads are used as photos; BIE must not reuse branded pages

verify before reuse: the table dates the switch to CPI-Combined at February 2015; RBI is usually said to have adopted CPI-Combined as its key inflation measure in April 2014, with the February 2015 monetary policy agreement formalising it

segments.teaches: title: the video compares headline inflation and core inflation

elements.what: two words 'INFLATION' side by side
bold black 'vs' between them
blue HEADLINE chip and purple CORE chip, each with a wavy underline, over the two words

segments.notes: 2 change events. Title card built in two beats: 'vs' on 'compare' (2.0 s), chips on 'headline inflation aur' (3.6 s).
segments.idea: there are two kinds of inflation figure and this video compares them
segments.shown_as: two identical INFLATION words face each other; a bold 'vs' pops between them, then a blue HEADLINE chip and a purple CORE chip with wavy underlines drop above each word

segments.teaches: an inflation index is built from many components; two of them, food and fuel, have prices that swing a lot for short-lived (transitory) reasons such as the season's rain

elements.what: 'INFLATION' label slides to the left edge as a row label; a second copy appears for the lower row

new kind (nothing fits): one horizontal strip, first plain yellow, then cut into seven pastel blocks of different widths, each block a component of the index basket; then duplicated as a second identical bar below
'INDEX' heading above the bar
two tall black frames, each spanning both bars around the same block
two pointer lines from the frames to a note: highly volatile and transitory in nature
FOOD written in the right framed block and FUEL in the left, in both bars

segments.notes: 8 change events, all in 10-31 s; then the canvas is still for about 34 s. 'segmented_bar' is a new element kind (an index basket drawn as a strip of blocks; not data). Transcript has no words from 12.6 to 24.4 s, so the bar, its copy and the frames are built over a pause or over lost speech. A further transcript gap at 41.3-46.6 s probably held a cause for fuel prices; not recovered.
segments.idea: the inflation index is a basket of parts; food and fuel are the parts whose prices jump around for temporary reasons
segments.shown_as: a yellow strip draws beside INFLATION, gets an INDEX heading and breaks into seven pastel blocks; the strip is copied into a second row; two black frames drop over the same two blocks in both rows, a forked pointer hangs a 'highly volatile & transitory' note under them, and the framed blocks are labelled FOOD and FUEL as each word is spoken; then nothing moves while the causes are told

segments.teaches: taking food and fuel out of the basket gives the core inflation index; the index that still includes them is the headline index; headline measures total inflation, core shows the long-run trend

elements.what: black frames and the volatile note removed
red crosses under FUEL and FOOD in the lower bar only
lower bar loses the two crossed blocks and closes up into a visibly shorter bar; upper bar stays full
purple CORE chip under the lower INFLATION label
blue HEADLINE chip over the upper INFLATION label

segments.notes: 5 change events in 65-89 s, each on its word (crosses on 'food aur fuel', shrink on 'bina food aur fuel', chips on 'core' and 'headline'); then about 23 s still while the difference is explained. Narration says 'food and energy' at 100 s while the screen says FUEL.
segments.idea: core inflation is the same basket with food and fuel removed; headline keeps everything
segments.shown_as: the frames lift; red crosses land under FUEL and FOOD in the lower bar as removal is spoken; the crossed blocks vanish and the remaining blocks slide together into a shorter bar; a purple CORE chip clips under the short bar's label and a blue HEADLINE chip over the full bar, leaving full vs trimmed basket stacked for comparison
segments.example: basket with 7 blocks vs basket with 5 blocks (food and fuel removed); no figures

segments.teaches: headline inflation is called 'headline' because it is the inflation rate most commonly reported in the media and newspaper headlines

elements.what: core row cleared; the HEADLINE bar slides down to the lower middle
three-line definition under HEADLINE INFLATION: the rate most commonly reported in media and headlines
two real newspaper front pages, an 'INFLATION' headline circled in yellow on each
two arrows from the papers converge on the word HEADLINE, then a curved arrow down to the HEADLINE chip

segments.notes: 3 change events. The definition text appears at 119.8 s while the question 'why is it called headline?' is still being asked; the spoken answer starts at 122.5 s. Newspaper mastheads are real brands: BIE must use generic papers.
segments.idea: 'headline' inflation is simply the number newspapers print
segments.shown_as: the core row disappears and the full HEADLINE bar slides down; a definition line writes on under it; above, two newspaper front pages appear with the inflation headline circled, and arrows run from both papers into the word HEADLINE and on down to the bar's HEADLINE chip

segments.teaches: India used WPI as its headline inflation measure till 2014 and CPI-Combined from February 2015

segments.idea: India's headline measure moved from wholesale prices to consumer prices
segments.shown_as: a small two-row table appears beside the newspapers: the WPI row dated 'till 2014' and the CPI-C row dated 'since Feb 2015', each with its full name; nothing points from it to the bar
